subject: drain-signals.js executes the real destructive drain on an UNRECOGNIZED flag (--help)

payload.mechanism: Unrecognized CLI flags fall through to the default action, which is the REAL drain (durable append + mv of files into docs/signals/processed/ + signals.db INSERT). There is no usage/help path and no unknown-flag rejection.

observed_live.effect: 5 signal files moved to docs/signals/processed/, 5 envelopes appended to .dev_team_idle_chain.pending_triage_inbox, signals.db db_count 565 -> 570
observed_live.intent: operator was reading usage, not draining

payload.why_it_matters: An operator or agent inspecting usage silently mutates the signal plane. In this instance the drain was wanted anyway so nothing was lost, but the same call on a tick where a drain was NOT wanted would move files out of the inbox mid-triage. Note the durable-append-before-destructive ordering held correctly throughout - this is a CLI-contract defect, not a data-integrity one.
candidate_directions: reject unknown flags with a non-zero exit and a usage block (safest, smallest)
require an affirmative --commit/--apply flag for the destructive path, making dry-run the default
not_duplicate_of: FIX-GUARD-SIGNAL-TYPE-COVERAGE-CHECK-MODE-MUTATES-BOARD-AND-DEDUPS-BY-KEY-NOT-SUBJECT (different script; that one's --check mode mutates, this one's unknown-flag fallback executes)
sys-20260825T170808-1ae7 (auditor-tier1-probe debounce cadence; that script mutates its own reported decision, also distinct)
payload.class_note: Third fleet script found in one session whose read-only-looking invocation is not read-only. The other two: auditor-tier1-probe.sh (a second run debounces against its own first run and returns a false DEBOUNCED, burning the spawn grant) and guard-signal-type-coverage.sh --check (auto-mints a board row and applies an orch-apply write). Worth considering whether a fleet-wide convention is the real fix rather than three separate patches.
